inputs.text: This isn’t just a technical rewrite of Cyprus’ surveillance laws. They’re trying to remove the judicial safeguard that could stop people from being monitored, while lawyers are warning about the changes and the amended bill is expected to go to a House vote on Thursday. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides’ mention of a recent closed session makes the pattern harder to ignore: decisions with serious consequences are being kept out of public view, then pushed through as routine reform. The secrecy is part of the point—it makes surveillance easier to expand and scrutiny easier to bypass.

output.main_topic: Proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance laws and concerns about weakened judicial oversight and secrecy
subtopics: Expected House vote on the amended bill
